plan.title: bug(hooks): a write outside every checkout is judged by the launching checkout's session ritual

narratives.Description: A Write or Edit to a file in the OS temp directory or an ordinary home folder outside every checkout is judged by the launching checkout's occupancy lease and session ritual, so a stale parent ritual or a foreign lease refuses a write that changes no checkout. This story adds a closed, fail-to-today class for such writes that skips occupancy, ritual, active scope and the story write fence while keeping the upstream gates, protected-store authz and runtime authority, and makes ritual refusals name the judged checkout with one runnable recovery command. It also renames the five temp-folder producers that lack `deft` and adds a unit test that keeps every Directive temp name under that rule.
narratives.Overview:
1. Two paths. For each direct-write target the class test builds the typed path (the target as given, normalized) and the complete physical destination. The physical destination is built by walking the typed path from its root one component at a time: each existing component is resolved with the operating system's native resolver (links, junctions, short names, letter case), and the first component that does not exist starts the unresolved rest, appended unchanged. An existing component that is a link whose target cannot be resolved makes the build fail.
2. Positive location. Both paths must be inside the physical OS temp directory, or inside a home directory. The home directories are the operating system's home directory and the values of `HOME` and `USERPROFILE`.
3. Configuration areas. A configuration area is a directory directly under a home directory whose name starts with a dot or is `Library` or `AppData` (any letter case), or a directory named by `APPDATA`, `LOCALAPPDATA`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME` or `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. For each path, the innermost directory that contains it, among all configuration areas and the OS temp directory, decides: when that innermost directory is a configuration area the path is not in the class; when it is the OS temp directory the path passes this item.
4. No repository and no Directive project. A filesystem walk from the deepest existing folder of the physical destination to the filesystem root finds no `.git` entry and no `.deft` entry beside any ancestor and no ancestor that is itself a Git directory. The Git toplevel lookup at that folder ran to completion and reported no repository. The target is outside the payload root by the existing `isOutsideProjectRootWrite` test.
5. Exclusions, on both paths, without regard to letter case. A path is not in the class when any component contains `deft` or `directive`, or is named `.git`; when it is equal to or inside the resolved value of any environment variable whose value is a path and whose name starts with `DEFT_` or `DIRECTIVE_`, or is one of `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME`, `GH_CONFIG_DIR`, `PNPM_HOME`, `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`; when it is inside any directory listed in `PATH`; or when it is inside the physical package directory of the Directive runtime that is running the hook.
6. Doubt rules, on both paths. Not in the class: a relative typed path; a component that ends with a dot or a space, has the Windows short-name form, or contains a colon after the drive prefix; a device or network-share prefix; a directory on the walk that cannot be read; a Git lookup that could not run or disagrees with the walk; a home directory or OS temp directory that cannot be resolved; an existing target file with more than one hard link.
7. A target that is not in the class is judged exactly as today. The class adds no deny. No existing authz or store check is edited.
8. Combining rule. `admitMutationTargetSet` runs first and unchanged. The class applies only when every target of the mutation is in it.
9. Gates for a set in the class. Upstream and unchanged: the kill switch, the read-only posture deny, the mutation intent ceiling and the Cursor planning-choice store check. Then protected-store authz and runtime authority run on the payload root, in the order the assist-scratch path runs them, and the write is allowed with its own decision code. The occupancy write gate, the gated session ritual, active scope and the story write fence do not run; the allow writes no product-mutation marker and does no write-gate lease refresh. The general owner-liveness renewal is unchanged. The class selects no ritual, lease, story or worktree registration and has no posture condition.
10. Recovery text. A direct write that is refused on the session ritual names the judged checkout and prints one recovery command that carries `--project-root <judged checkout>` and runs as printed.
11. Docs. `content/docs/hook-root-admission.md` states the class and its rules, and says that the ritual requirement is removed for the class on purpose and what that gives up. It states the naming rule for Directive code: a file or folder that Directive keeps outside a checkout has `deft` or `directive` in its name or in a parent folder name, or lives in a configuration area, or is named by a `DEFT_` or `DIRECTIVE_` environment variable.
12. Temp names. Every file or folder that Directive code creates under the OS temp directory has `deft` in its created name. The producers that lack it at the dispatch SHA are renamed: `mge-put-` in `packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/gh.ts`, `gh_rest_payload_` in `packages/core/src/scm/gh-rest.ts`, `release-proj-` in `packages/core/src/release/pipeline-fixture.ts`, the tutorial repository prefix in `packages/core/src/tutorial/cli.ts`, and the caller-supplied prefix in `packages/core/src/integration-e2e/helpers.ts`. One unit test in this repository's suite reads the non-test source under `packages/core/src`, `packages/runtime/src` and `packages/cli/src` and fails when a temp-directory file or folder is created with a name that lacks `deft`.
narratives.Constraint:
- A temp-directory exception that outranks the configuration-area rule (comment 6908510670 finding 1).
- A list of named Directive stores as the exclusion.
- Editing the existing authz or planning-choice store checks in this story.
- Choosing a worker's ritual, lease or story from the write target or from a worktree registration (#6334 panel).
- Returning no effective root for an out-of-tree target (#4013).
- A posture condition, a stored allowlist of folders or a new operator setting for this class.
- Any change to shell or MCP write classification.
narratives.UserStory: As an agent or worker whose launching checkout has a stale session ritual or a foreign lease, I want a Write or Edit to a file in the OS temp directory or an ordinary home folder outside every checkout to be allowed without that ritual, and a ritual refusal to name the checkout it judged with one runnable recovery command, so that a write that changes no checkout does not stop me.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Add `packages/core/src/hooks/outside-every-checkout.ts`: the class test (typed path and physical destination, positive location, configuration areas with the innermost rule, repository and Directive-project walk plus the Git toplevel lookup, exclusions, doubt rules), with injectable seams for tests, and the `deftTempName` helper. 2. In `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` `inspectMutationGates`, after `admitMutationTargetSet` and the assist-scratch block, allow a bare direct write whose every target is in the class: authz then runtime authority on the payload root, decision code `write-outside-every-checkout-ready`, before occupancy, ritual, scope and fence. 3. Make ritual-not-ready denials name the judged checkout and print one `session:start` command with `--project-root <judged checkout>`. 4. Rename the five temp producers and add the temp-name unit test to `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher-outside-root.test.ts`. 5. Update `content/docs/hook-root-admission.md`, the #4013 characterization tests and CHANGELOG.

## In plain English
When an agent writes a file with the Write or Edit tool, a hook decides whether to allow it. For a file that is not inside any checkout (a notes folder, the OS temp directory, an agent memory folder), the hook has no checkout to judge it by, so it falls back to the checkout the session started in. That checkout's session ritual and occupancy lease then decide. If that ritual has gone stale, the write is refused, although the file is in no checkout and no product file changes. Workers hit this most: their own worktree is ready, and the stale ritual belongs to the parent. #4013 kept this fallback on purpose and wrote down what a narrowing would have to define. The candidate is that narrowing: treat a write that is proven to be outside every checkout as its own class that skips occupancy and ritual, like assist scratch does, and keep every other gate. The open question is whether that class can be proven safely, and whether skipping the two gates lets anything through that they stopped for a reason.

## Pains
- P1 — A Write or Edit whose every target is outside every checkout is refused when the launching checkout's session ritual is stale or its lease is held by another session, although the write changes no checkout. A worker cannot fix it by re-arming its own worktree.
- P2 — When a write is refused on a session ritual, the printed recovery does not name the checkout that was judged, so the worker runs it in the wrong checkout.
- P3 — A fix must keep today's result for a target inside a checkout, inside a Git directory or inside a protected store, and must not let a write target or a worktree registration select a ritual, a lease or a story.

## Out of this arc

- Relative-target canonicalization in general (#4023). The candidate must say how it avoids depending on it.
- Worker scratch inside the worker's own worktree, launch and close-out (#6334).
- Auto re-arm of a stale ritual (#6279).

An unrelated notes-file write can currently be blocked by the launching checkout’s stale session ritual. The candidate removes that coupling, but its claim that no protected control is lost does not hold as written.

My answers to the three questions are:

- **C1 does not yet prove the class.** A failed Git lookup can mean that Git could not inspect a repository, rather than that no repository exists.
- **C3 drops an existing readiness requirement.** Ordinary home and configuration writes would no longer require verified hook readiness or the recorded doctor check. Assist scratch already has an exemption, but it also requires an explicit assist or ephemeral posture.
- **Skipping occupancy and ritual together avoids their partial-transition problem.** However, returning early does not prevent the outer hook callback from renewing the owner’s lease.

The proposal can remain a deliberate narrowing of policy, but it cannot bind on the present proof or on an assertion of unchanged controls.

All code evidence below was read with `git show` at `72fe1658a04cef37d4dbea2bdad46ca087721853`. No files were changed, tests run, or posts made.

### 1. blocks-the-design — Git failure is not evidence of absence

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/session/git.ts:62–93` represents missing Git, sandbox execution failures and other subprocess failures as nonzero results. Its `worktreePathOrNull` at lines 262–269 collapses every nonzero result into `null`. `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1271–1274` admits that null result against the payload root; the `unproven-identity` refusal at lines 1284–1286 applies only after a toplevel was successfully found.

**Failure mode:** An absolute target in another checkout can be physically resolved and lie outside the payload root while Git inspection fails. Unchanged admission falls back to the payload root. If C1 interprets the same failed lookup as “no toplevel” and a failed `--git-dir` as “outside Git,” the target gains the exemption despite residing inside a checkout. A sandbox failure is already an explicitly represented case; this requires no adversarial race.

**Disposition consequence:** C1 needs a distinction between established absence and inability to inspect. Unknown results must retain today’s gate path. C2’s existing refusals cannot supply that distinction because the null fallback precedes them.

### 2. blocks-the-design — The assist-scratch analogy omits a control and broadens the exemption

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1132–1147` requires both an allowlisted scratch path and assist or ephemeral classification; its comment explicitly says path alone fails closed. `packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts:198–214` requires `agent_hooks` and `doctor` for write gating. `dispatcher.ts:2333–2355` performs that verification, and lines 2420–2441 refuse a failed ritual.

**Failure mode:** A normal mutation session with no valid ritual can write an ordinary non-protected home/configuration file under C1–C3, provided the retained authorization checks allow it. The destination alone now selects exemption from readiness verification. An absolute path copied from untrusted issue content can trigger this behavior without the posture condition required for assist scratch.

This is the concrete control loss identified in `content/docs/hook-root-admission.md:47–52`. It is not a claim that the ritual authenticates user intent or that occupancy serializes all external files.

**Disposition consequence:** The refutation target’s “without dropping a control” premise is false. A bindable design must expressly accept removal of this readiness requirement for ordinary external writes, or retain a narrower eligibility condition. Selecting no alternate ritual or story does not make that policy change disappear.

### 3. sharpens-framing — Early allow still permits owner-liveness renewal

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:2070–2074` records the admitted effective root before the scratch-style early return. **Failure mode:** An owner writes an eligible external note, receives the proposed early allow, and still refreshes the launching checkout’s heartbeat. Clearing the recorded roots alone would not stop this because the callback falls back to the payload root. This is owner-only liveness renewal, not borrowing another session’s ritual or recording a product write.

**Disposition consequence:** C3 must distinguish skipping the write-gate lease refresh from skipping all lease renewal. Preserving ordinary owner liveness is coherent and leaves no half-completed occupancy/ritual transition, but the current blanket “lease re-stamp does not run” description is inaccurate.

Problem: a Write or Edit to a file that is in no checkout (a notes folder, the OS temp directory, an agent memory folder) is judged by the checkout the session started in. The candidate said no control is lost, and that is false: a session with no valid ritual could then write an ordinary file outside the checkouts, which today needs a ritual. And the candidate said the lease is not re-stamped, but the general "owner is alive" renewal still runs on every hook event.

Solution this lean proposes: add one class of direct write, "outside every checkout", that is allowed without the occupancy gate and without the session ritual. A target is in the class only when two independent checks agree that it is in no checkout and no Git directory; any doubt keeps today's behaviour. Protected stores, the kill switch, the read-only posture and the intent ceiling still apply. The lean says plainly that the ritual requirement is removed for this class and why. A ritual refusal that still happens names the checkout that was judged.

What it removes: the ritual and lease refusal for a write that touches no checkout.

What it does not do: it does not change a write to any file inside a checkout, a Git directory or a protected store. It does not cover shell or MCP writes, which never reached this check. It does not let a worker write product files without a ritual, because a product file is inside a checkout and is therefore never in the class. If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design. - It does not cover shell or MCP writes.
- It does not let a worker write product files without a ritual, because a product file is inside a checkout and is never in the class.

## In plain English

Problem: a Write or Edit to a file in the OS temp directory, or in an ordinary folder under the home directory, was judged by the checkout the session started in. When that checkout's session ritual was stale, or another session held its lease, the write was refused, although no checkout and no configuration changed. A worker could not fix it from its own worktree, and the refusal did not say which checkout was judged.

Accepted solution: one new class of direct write, allowed without the occupancy gate and without the session ritual. A write is in the class only when its physical destination is inside the OS temp directory, or inside a home directory and not in a configuration area; when a path is inside both, the innermost decides. No path in a checkout, a Git directory or a Directive project is in the class, nor any path with `deft` or `directive` in a folder or file name, nor any path that a Directive environment variable points at. Any path form the test cannot read with certainty is kept out, and a target kept out is judged exactly as today. The temp folders that Directive creates all get `deft` in their names. A ritual refusal that still happens names the checkout that was judged and prints one command with `--project-root`.

The deliberate choice: for a write in the class, Write and Edit no longer need a session ritual, as shell writes to the same files already do not. A session with no valid ritual could not do that with those tools before and can afterwards.

The design adds no new gate, refusal, approval or stored state. Limits accepted: a file in a configuration area, such as an agent memory folder under a host's dot-folder, and a folder outside the home and temp directories, stay judged as today and no issue carries them; the path-form rules were checked by source reading only and need tests on each operating system. No leftover next-build.

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

A Write or Edit to a path outside every checkout (a notes folder, a host scratchpad, an agent memory folder) is judged by the session ritual of the checkout the hook started in. When that ritual is stale, the write is refused, although it changes nothing in any checkout. In-session workers hit this most: their own worktree ritual is fresh, and the stale one belongs to the parent.

Split from #6334 (pain P2 remainder) by operator decision on 2026-11-16. The #6334 design moves relocatable worker notes and scratch into the worker's own worktree and stops the instructed cwd drift. This issue carries the case that design does not cover: a file that has to stay outside every checkout.

## What we saw

1. `admitEffectiveHookRoot` (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`) falls back to the payload root when the write target has no Git toplevel. That fallback is deliberate (#4013, `content/docs/hook-root-admission.md`).
2. The gated session ritual of that root then judges the write, before the outside-root skip of the active-scope check is reached.
3. In wave 2a (2026-11-15/16) worker writes to a notes folder were refused on a parent ritual that had gone stale by age or by a HEAD switch. Re-arming the worker's own worktree did not help, because the stale ritual was the parent's.
4. The parent's own out-of-tree writes are judged by whichever checkout its shell cwd is in at that moment.
5. The #6334 design-critique panel (three critic families and a pain-audit) agreed that a worktree registration must not be used to choose which worker's ritual judges such a write: the target names no worker.

## Constraints from #4013

- Returning no root for an out-of-tree write would drop ritual, occupancy, active scope and the write fence together.
- Occupancy and ritual are cross-checked, and an allowed write re-stamps the lease.
- A write target must not become an input that selects authority.
- Protected-store authorization and the kill switch stay on the payload root.

## Expected

Fewer stops: a write that touches no checkout is not refused for a stale ritual when no control that the ritual protects is in play, or the design shows why the ritual is needed there and makes the recovery one command that runs as printed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a stale ritual in the launching checkout and a write whose every target is outside every checkout and outside every protected store, when the hook evaluates the write, then the result follows a rule that is written down for that case.
- Given the same write, when the rule refuses it, then the refusal prints one recovery command that names the judged checkout and runs as printed.
- Given a write whose target is inside a checkout or a protected store, when the hook evaluates it, then the result is the same as today.
- The rule does not select a ritual, a lease or a story from the write target or from a worktree registration.
- `content/docs/hook-root-admission.md` states the rule and the reason for it.

Refs #6334. Refs #4013. Refs #6279.
